flagged.evidence: It defines a prescribed part as \(\sum_{m=1}^{M}c_{-m}(z-a)^{-m}\), then says this is “exactly the shape of the principal part of a pole of order \(M\).” No condition \(c_{-M}\ne0\) is imposed. Taking \(c_{-M}=0\) gives a part of order at most \(M-1\) (or zero), not one from a pole of order \(M\).

The step infers from \(a_{j-1},a_j\in D(c,\rho)\) that \(|a_{j-1}-a_j|<\rho<|z-a_j|\) for every \(z\in K\). The first inequality is false. For \(K=\{1.1\}\), \(\overline D(0,1)\cap K=\varnothing\), \(a_{j-1}=-0.99\), and \(a_j=0.99\), the stated chain condition holds but \(|a_{j-1}-a_j|=1.98\), while \(|1.1-a_j|=0.11\). Thus the claimed geometric series need not converge on \(K\).

The hypotheses require only \(|a_n|\to\infty\), but the proof chooses \(|a_n|<R_n<|a_{n+1}|\). This can fail: enumerate \(A=\{\pm1,\pm2,\ldots\}\) as \(1,-1,2,-2,\ldots\); then \(|a_n|\to\infty\), yet no \(R_1\) satisfies \(1<R_1<1\). A grouped-shell construction is needed.

The cited \(\texttt{thm-runge-approximation-on-plane-domains}\) applies to a function \(f:\Omega\to\mathbb C\) holomorphic on all of \(\Omega\). Here \(g_n\) is explicitly a finite sum of principal parts and has poles at the points of \(A_n\subset\Omega\); step 1.1 only makes it holomorphic near \(K_{n-1}\). Therefore [L2] does not license approximating \(g_n\) as asserted.

The proof says \(\pi\cot(\pi z)\) is bounded on the closed strip \(1/2\le\operatorname{Re}z\le3/2\) “away from its poles,” then concludes that \(g\) is bounded on that strip. But the strip contains the pole \(z=1\); the series \(h\) has the same pole, so boundedness of their difference requires a cancellation argument that is not given. The displayed assertion does not establish the Liouville hypothesis.

For the defined orientation (lower ray from radial infinity to 0, then counterclockwise, then upper ray outwards), the ray contributions are \(e^{\pi iz}\Gamma(1-z)\) and \(-e^{-\pi iz}\Gamma(1-z)\). Their sum is \(+2i\sin(\pi z)\Gamma(1-z)\), not the written \(-2i\sin(\pi z)\Gamma(1-z)\). With [L1], the written negative quantity equals \(-2\pi i/\Gamma(z)\), contradicting step 3.1’s claimed positive value.

From [L1], writing \(S=\sum_{n\ge1}(\log(1+z/n)-z/n)\), one has \(\log\Gamma(z)=-\log z-\gamma z-S\). For the defined \(F\), this gives \(\log F=-S-\gamma z+z-\tfrac12\log(2\pi)-(z+\tfrac12)\operatorname{Log}z\). Step 1.1 instead writes \(+S+z\log z-z+\tfrac12\log z-\tfrac12\log(2\pi)-\gamma z\), with incompatible signs and powers, so step 2.1 does not follow.
